rules: The design source defines seven token roles at 40, 40, 28, 36, 24, 16, and 16 px; the smallest source-defined role is 16 px.
Montserrat and Oswald roles are uppercase; Merriweather roles are mixed or sentence case.
Display, heading, and CTA use TextScaled with token size as a maximum; body, caption, and label use fixed TextSize.
Line height is not authored in the design source, Theme, representative components, or inspected stories; it is null rather than inferred.
Ordinary text has no outline. The source assigns a 1 px contextual dark rim to gradient display digits; the ShopOffers implementation also applies that rim to its gradient banner headline.
Dark-surface text uses candle cream, rose parchment, or dim taupe; bright cream/gold/salmon controls use dark chocolate, amber, or maroon ink.
exceptions: The generated ItemRow title reuses the 40 px heading face but caps it at 24 px, 0.6 of the heading token.
The generated ItemRow tier caption reuses the 28 px eyebrow face at 14 px, exactly 0.5 of the token and 2 px below the source design minimum.
Rendered minimum is unavailable: TextScaled roles have only MaxTextSize constraints and no MinTextSize constraint, so responsive containers can render them below their authored maxima.
The ShopOffers banner applies the 1 px text rim to a headline, while the source prose specifically motivates the rim for gradient digits.
The source component tokens specify pure white for button-secondary text and card-grid text, contradicting the prose rule that text should never be pure white.

hierarchy.observed: A screen may contain at most one dominant cream-filled primary CTA. It uses a 36 px uppercase condensed label, a 5:1 silhouette, no stroke, and no shadow; other launchers remain dark, outlined tiles.
hierarchy.designFunction: Concentrates primary action salience in a single large light surface while preserving the one-ink palette elsewhere.

hierarchy.observed: The nominal window hierarchy is 40 px serif title, 28 px uppercase section eyebrow, 40 px display offer headline with 16 px caption, 24 px price/action label, and 16 px serif body or hint. The source orders window content header row → section label → banner → card row → next section.
hierarchy.designFunction: Separates parlor narration, merchandise categories, offer emphasis, and transactional labels through face, size, casing, and sequence.

hierarchy.observed: The dialog orders a 40 px maximum serif title, then 16 px serif sentence-case body, then one cream primary CTA whose label can scale up to 36 px; dismissal remains the bare header X instead of a second filled action.
hierarchy.designFunction: Keeps confirmation dominant without introducing a competing filled cancel control.

hierarchy.observed: The design source defines 15 named color roles but 14 unique named hex values because primary and outline both equal #FFDEBC. The base system contains warm-plum surfaces, one cream ink, a gold commerce family, and a rose life/exit family.
hierarchy.designFunction: Provides semantic role separation without expanding the neutral ink family.

hierarchy.observed: Cream #FFDEBC is reused for ordinary bright text, glyphs, strokes, gauges, and the one dominant CTA fill. Non-CTA hierarchy is expressed through size, opacity, typography, and stroke brightness rather than additional brand hues.
hierarchy.designFunction: Maintains a single candlelight visual motif while allowing the CTA to invert surface and ink.

hierarchy.observed: Commerce uses chestnut #623A27, gold #FAD594, and amber ink #8E552D; life/revive uses rose well #522227, salmon #F45665, soft rose #FEB2B7, and maroon ink #732327. ShopOffers keeps gold on the boost banner and rose on revive pills. Category meaning is strongly hue-coded, but text labels, section placement, pill/surface pairings, and dark family-specific ink also distinguish the two systems, so hue is not the only signal in the inspected offer story.
hierarchy.designFunction: Separates spending from life/exit contexts while retaining dark-ink-on-bright-pill contrast treatment.

hierarchy.observed: Surface/ink pairs are warm rather than neutral: near-black plum #1A0F10 with cream #FFDEBC or parchment #EAB6A3; cream fill with chocolate #402419; gold fill #FAD594 with amber #8E552D; salmon #F45665 with maroon #732327. Placeholder and tertiary text use #907A74.
hierarchy.designFunction: Creates primary, secondary, and tertiary contrast treatments while avoiding neutral black for normal source-defined pairings.

hierarchy.observed: Two source component entries break the prose prohibition on pure white text: button-secondary textColor and card-grid textColor are both #FFFFFF.

Depth uses translucent warm-dark fills, lightened inset wells, and 1–3 px lit edges. Window transparency is 0.08, HUD chrome transparency is 0.20, standard outlines are 2 px, tiny-tag outlines are 3 px, ambient HUD outlines are 3 px at 0.70 transparency, and contextual text rims are 1 px. Shadows and bevels are explicitly absent.
hierarchy.designFunction: Uses world bleed-through and edge luminance rather than cast shadows as elevation cues.

hierarchy.observed: The radius ladder is 8, 12, and 20 px plus full rounding reserved for progress strips. Cards, tags, banner wells, and price controls use 8 px; CTAs, inputs, hotbar slots, and the generated window use 12 px; launcher tiles alone use 20 px. Buttons remain rounded rectangles, price controls are not capsules, and circular silhouettes are absent from the source.
hierarchy.designFunction: Keeps silhouettes consistently axis-aligned while reserving the largest curve for launchers and full rounding for narrow gauges.

hierarchy.observed: The source prose describes the window shell as measured near 10 px and assigns it to the small-radius grouping, while the front-matter window token and generated ParlorWindow use rounded.md = 12 px.

Source product cards are the only major strokeless artwork surfaces: 0.10-transparent vertical gradient, 8 px corners, and no edge. Generated ItemRow preserves that surface treatment but changes the silhouette from a roughly 0.92:1 card to an 84 px-high full-width strip; emphasized Crown also receives a brighter gold gradient and a 1 px title rim.
hierarchy.designFunction: Distinguishes merchandise artwork from outlined window chrome while allowing a single top-item emphasis.

hierarchy.observed: The source spacing ladder is 4, 8, 16, and 28 px. Adjacent multipliers are 2.0, 2.0, and 1.75. The assigned uses are 4 px hairline gaps, 8 px icon/label and title-cluster gaps, 16 px default sibling gaps, and 28 px window padding and inter-section gaps.
hierarchy.designFunction: Establishes a four-step rhythm that separates internal micro-gaps, sibling groups, and section/window boundaries.

hierarchy.observed: Visible and interactive targets are distinct for price and close controls. The BuyPill is 36 px high inside a transparent 44 px touch root; the close glyph is 24 px inside a 44 px touch frame. Launchers are 68 px and source hotbar slots are approximately 112 px.
hierarchy.designFunction: Preserves compact visual controls while expanding their interactive frames.

hierarchy.observed: The generated Shop catalog uses six 84 px full-width rows with 12 px gaps in a scrolling column. Each row has 16 px horizontal and 8 px vertical padding, a 60 px render well, a 4 px title/tier gap, and a 44 px buy target. The 12 px row gap is not a member of the 4/8/16/28 source ladder.
hierarchy.designFunction: Increases catalog information density relative to the source three-card row while retaining the source's strip grammar and internal spacing tokens.

hierarchy.observed: The source-observed HUD composition is limited to a bottom-center hotbar: numbered square slots, top-left overlapping key tags, a smaller trailing overflow slot, a cream underline rail, and at most three persistent data items per slot—keybind, quantity, and durability. Currency, objectives, side buttons, and the rest of the HUD were not observed.
hierarchy.designFunction: Concentrates persistent inventory information in a bounded bottom-center zone while limiting per-slot content.

hierarchy.observed: The generated HUD story adds a top-left passive currency pill, three labeled 163×68 launchers in a top-right row with 16 px gaps, and a 340×68 primary CTA at bottom-center. It queries live top inset and leaves bottom-left and bottom-right clear. These zones are implementation additions because the source lacked a full HUD map and explicitly left currency-bar undefined.
hierarchy.designFunction: Creates a showcase HUD composition while avoiding the conventional touch-control corners.

hierarchy.observed: The source Shop is a single panel with no tabs or rail. Reading order is header title/utility/input/close, then section eyebrow plus hint, full-width offer banner, and a row of three product cards with Back occupying the first card slot. The generated standard Shop replaces sections and card rows with one scrolling column of six strips.
hierarchy.designFunction: The source sequence moves from window identity and utilities to category context, featured offer, then individual products; the implementation prioritizes standard-catalog comparability.

hierarchy.observed: The dialog is not a source-defined bespoke object. The implementation reuses ParlorWindow at 420×220, centers it above a full-screen dim layer, keeps the title and bare X in a 52 px header, and stacks body then confirm with a 16 px gap. Popup Z order is dim 10 then panel 11, matching the source ordering dim → window → floating text.
hierarchy.designFunction: Focuses the modal by reusing the established window anatomy and removing unrelated controls.

hierarchy.observed: World visibility is source-authored through a warm-plum window at 0.08 transparency and dark HUD chrome at 0.20 transparency. The source confirms a dimmed world behind Shop but could not isolate dim opacity. The generated stories add a #221514 stand-in world and a black dim layer at 0.55 transparency; both values are implementation additions rather than observed tokens.
hierarchy.designFunction: Allows environmental imagery to remain present behind UI while the modal wash isolates foreground content.

hierarchy.observed: No default/hover/focus/pressed/disabled/selected state variants were observed in the source screenshots, and no video was supplied. The source motion block is explicitly an unmodified taste-family preset, not observed motion.

The generated motion register uses Sine easing with 0.10 s instant, 0.25 s fast, 0.45 s normal, and 0.80 s slow durations. ParlorWindow enters by fading from GroupTransparency 1 while sliding from +0.02 normalized Y over 0.45 s Sine Out, and exits by fading over 0.25 s Sine In. These are generated implementations of the preset, not source-observed motion.
hierarchy.designFunction: Keeps modal transitions fade-led and avoids scale overshoot or bounce.

hierarchy.observed: Generated interactive controls add a brightness lift on press and 0.45 transparency for disabled. Bright and dark fills move 12% toward white or cream; ItemRow changes background transparency from 0.10 to 0.02 on press. Release and MouseLeave restore default over 0.25 s. Disabled controls suppress activation and dim fill/text. Hover has no distinct entered state, focus has no visual treatment, and selected is not implemented.
hierarchy.designFunction: Communicates pressing through luminance rather than hue or geometry and communicates disabled state through opacity rather than hue alone.

hierarchy.observed: The bare close glyph alone gets a press color lift from #FFDEBC to the derived 12%-toward-white value, then restores on release. There is no disabled, hover-enter, keyboard-focus, or selected treatment for close.
hierarchy.designFunction: Preserves the containerless close silhouette while adding minimal press acknowledgment.

openQuestions: What are the intended line heights for all typography roles? No line-height value is authored anywhere inspected.
What is the true minimum rendered text size across supported viewports? TextScaled roles have maxima but no minima, so the value cannot be derived from source.
Are the 14 px generated item-tier captions intentional despite being half the 28 px eyebrow token and below the source's 16 px minimum role?
Should gradient banner headlines carry the 1 px text rim, or should the rim remain limited to gradient digits as the source prose states?
Should the window use 8, approximately 10, or 12 px corners? The prose grouping, measured note, front-matter component token, and generated implementation do not agree.
What is the actual full-viewport HUD zone map? Only the bottom-center hotbar crop was observed; currency, objectives, side buttons, and launcher placement remain unobserved.
What black-wash opacity should modal dimming use? The source confirms dimming but could not isolate it; 0.55 transparency is generated.
Should the standard Shop preserve the source three-card section anatomy or the generated six-row scrolling catalog? Both are present inside this taste.
Should hover, keyboard/gamepad focus, and selected states be visually distinct? None were observed or generated.

The 420×220 dialog has 28 px top/bottom window padding, a 52 px header, and a 16 px header/content gap, leaving 96 px of content height; its body 48 px + stack gap 16 px + CTA 56 px totals 120 px. Is clipping or a taller dialog intended?
All extracted pixel sizes may share a constant-factor error because the source crops had unknown viewport scale; the design source explicitly records this normalization caveat.
